items.summary: Every animal has its own table, and its table decides where it lives and what it does. After reading this, you can sort animals into plant-eaters, meat-eaters and mixed-eaters, watch for the signs that tell you what an animal eats, and explain why plants and animals depend on each other.
items.title: What Do Animals Eat?

items.summary: A farm is a busy place where animals live, work and eat. After reading this you can name the animals you will meet on a farm, use the words farmers use every day, and visit a farm without frightening anybody.
items.title: Meet the Animals on the Farm

items.summary: Insects are small, but they are everywhere and they do enormous work. After reading this, you can spot an insect by its three body parts and six legs, learn what insects do for us, and watch them closely without hurting them.
items.title: The Wonderful World of Insects

items.summary: Birds build nests for four good reasons, and every species has its own design. After reading this you can say what a nest is for, name the parts of an egg, recognise six kinds of nest, and watch birds without disturbing them.
items.title: Why Do Birds Build Nests?

items.summary: The ocean covers most of our planet, and every part of it is full of life. After reading this you can name the animals that live in each zone of the sea, use the words scientists use for them, and stay safe when you visit the beach.
items.title: Life Under the Ocean

items.summary: A pet is an animal that lives with you and depends on you every day. After reading this, you can tell what different pets need, feed and care for one properly, and know the safety rules that keep both you and the animal well.
items.title: Pets and How to Care for Them

items.summary: The savanna is a great open grassland full of grass eaters and hungry hunters. After reading this you can name the animals that live there, use the words scientists use for them, and explain what happens on a savanna in the space of one day.
items.title: Amazing Animals of the African Savanna

items.summary: Most children have an animal they love most. After reading this you can name your favourite animal, say where it lives and what it eats, and describe an animal so well that somebody else can picture it.
items.title: Talking About Your Favorite Animals

items.summary: Bedtime is a routine, and a routine is a set of small steps you repeat every night. After reading this you can get ready for bed in the right order, say the bedtime words, talk with your family before sleep, and calm down when you cannot fall asleep.
items.title: Getting Ready for Bedtime

items.summary: A friend at school is someone you meet, talk to, and play with again and again. After reading this you can say hello to a new child, join a game, find something you both like, and keep a new friendship going.
items.title: Making Friends at School

items.summary: A good question is a small key that opens a big door. After reading this you can ask a clear question in class, use the right question words, wait for your turn, and ask a teacher or grown-up for help politely.
items.title: Asking Questions in the Classroom

items.summary: The weather is the easiest subject in the world to talk about, because everybody has one. After reading this you can describe the sky, tell how hot or cold it is, say what the weather is like, and choose the right clothes for the day.
items.title: Talking About the Weather

items.summary: A good friend listens, shares, tells the truth, and stays close. After reading this you can pick a good friend, be a good friend yourself, and fix a friendship after a quarrel.
items.title: What Makes a Good Friend?

items.summary: Asking for help is a skill, not a weakness. After reading this, you can try first, ask clearly, say what kind of help you need, and tell a grown-up straight away when something is really wrong.
items.title: How to Ask for Help

items.summary: Bread is flour and water and a tiny yeast. After reading this you can name the four ingredients, explain why bread rises, bake a simple loaf at home, and tell the difference between kinds of bread.
items.title: How Bread Is Made

items.summary: Breakfast is the first meal of the day. After reading this you can say what breakfast is for, name breakfasts from around the world, and make a simple breakfast for yourself at home.
items.title: What's for Breakfast?

items.summary: The bathroom holds the things that keep us clean and well. After reading this, you can name the things in a bathroom, wash your hands the right way, and stay safe near water, hot water and sharp things.
items.title: Things We Use in the Bathroom

items.summary: Everything around you has a shape and a colour. After reading this, you can name the common shapes and colours, find them in your home and your street, and use them to draw and build your own pictures.
items.title: Learning About Shapes and Colors

items.summary: A toy is something we play with, and every toy has a way to play with it. After reading this, you can name the toys around you, choose the right game for each toy, play well with friends, and keep your toys in good shape.
items.title: Toys and How We Play With Them

items.summary: Attachment styles describe the promises a person brings to a partner, the way they read availability, and what they do when a partner is unavailable. After reading this you can name the four styles, describe what each one looks for and fears, recognise the signals that switch your own pattern on, and say what you need in words your partner can act on.
items.title: Attachment Styles in Romantic Relationships

items.summary: An average difference between two groups says where the centres of two clouds sit, not where any one person stands. After reading this you can name the five parts of emotional maturity, say what a claim about men and women can and cannot tell you about one person, read a group claim without turning it into a rule, and hold a conversation about it without the argument becoming a fight.
items.title: Gender Differences in Emotional Maturity

items.summary: Mate selection is the process of choosing a partner, and it has its own vocabulary. After reading this you can separate attraction, preference and decision, describe how people actually choose, read the direction and the size of an age gap, and run a short check on the preferences you say you hold.
items.title: Mate Selection and Age Preferences

items.summary: Persuasion is ordinary in a negotiation; the dark part is using it to hide the real price, the real stock or the real deadline. After reading this you can name nine techniques, say what the honest version of the same request is, and prepare the two things that protect you: your alternative and your walk-away price.
items.title: Dark Psychology in Business and Negotiation
